human_lessons.distinction: Offering a rook is effective because the bishop remains; refusing with Qd2 changes the magnitude of the advantage. A winning acceptance line is insufficient.
The opponent has a perpetual-check resource before the natural improvement; the preparatory queen move must be understood through that response, including the stronger g5 counter.
Three moves stop the pawn, but only Re8 retains the win. Functional family membership does not certify interchangeable value.
A defensive resource must survive the strongest refusal Rc8 as well as tempting pawn pushes.
A tactical saving resource after the opponent blunders does not establish that the earlier move caused the blunder.
A rook activity principle explains the task; counting pawns alone does not explain why the opponent king must take over the blockade.
